name: PA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Reschenthaler with large financial advantage ($4.2M raised vs $201K)
Prediction markets price Republican win at 98%
No polls or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean, Reschenthaler's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising edge, and markets pricing a 98% Republican win all point to a safe Republican hold. No polls or ratings justify moving away from that picture.
model.watch: A late Democratic outside-spending surge or unexpected incumbent scandal could narrow the margin, though a genuine upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Guy Reschenthaler seeks another term in a southwestern Pennsylvania district that leans strongly Republican, about 17 points to the right of the country overall. He enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $4.2 million to challenger Alan Bradstock's $201,000, and holds nearly $1 million on hand with no meaningful outside spending against him.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, and those all point one way: the district lean, incumbency, money, and prediction markets pricing a Republican win at 98 percent. Bradstock faces an uphill contest with limited resources.
